title: Leaving Louis Armstrong because his wife was ill
summary: After 12 years with Armstrong, he left in 1964 to care for his wife, who had cancer, and Joe Glaser was angry.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So, yeah, I stayed with Louis until '64, and this is -- well, I knew my wife was sick, but I didn't know what was wrong with her. I'd bought a home in the meantime here in Los Angeles, and her and my daughter were living here. So I just would commute. You know, when I had told you how much time you get off with Louis, you know. I would come back and visit, and so finally when I found my wife was sick, I left the band, and Joe Glazer got so mad with me, he hardly spoke to me, you know, about that, because he wanted to give me more money.

I said, no, I got to go home. My wife is sick. And so it's a good thing I did because I found out my wife had cancer, and we caught it, you know, just in time. She went out to this White Memorial Hospital out here, and I used to take her out there for cobalt treatments.

And so this was May of '64. See, I stayed with Louis from 1952 to about February of -- first part of '64. And after she completed her treatments, the doctor said, well, there's no more I can do. We just have to wait and see how

she comes along. So they gave us permission to move, and we -- I sold my home. We went back to Honolulu, and I'd been living back there since, you know, but I found out that, had I stayed on the road and accepted more money, well, my wife would have been gone, you know?
But this is how the guys like Glaser, they measure everything in dollars and cents, you know.
